blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **The Tracker Handoff and Dynamic Reference Envelopes**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Safety Enforcement, § The Tracker Handoff and Dynamic Reference Envelopes
blocks.md: Even when communication latency is zero and the permission path admits every reference command without delay, physical robots follow reference trajectories imperfectly. Mechanical compliance, inertia, and non-ideal motor dynamics produce tracking discrepancies. The feedback tracker, the closed-loop controller that turns admitted references into actuator effort, must bound this deviation across the entire maneuver. The bound is a **worst-case tracking error tube** (TrackingErrorBound), an upper bound on the spatial departure of the tracked position output from its nominal reference.

questions.q: The section **The Tracker Handoff and Dynamic Reference Envelopes** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: The stopping envelope is the set of states from which the resident stop, after every worst-case delay, halts before the obstacle with localization, protective, and tracking margins intact, and its seven priced rows run as a per-tick speed governor.
The feedback tracker guarantees a worst-case tracking tube only inside its qualified envelope, so the enforcer insets every clearance by it and watches the premises that keep it true.
Available deceleration is net of gravity and bias in the worst direction, and integrator unwinding and saturation spend it before the stop begins.

A series compliance, whose stiffness falls below that of its softer element because compliances add, slows the force rise and bounds impact force passively when the enforcer cannot stop in time, so its stiffness is part of the contact margin.
